facts.fact: UNDP reports that SIREC was implemented with UNDP technical assistance and financed by the Swiss Confederation, the European Union and Portuguese Cooperation; no domestic funding is mentioned.

UNDP reports that during 2025 it deployed the SIREC platform, trained 63 civil registry officials on digital systems, and that Decree No. 02/2025 set a new legal framework for digital civil registration.

systems.owner: Ministry of Justice and Human Rights civil registration service; deployed by UNDP
systems.tiers: civil registry offices and health facilities, as designed; no count of offices given
Bissau: all civil birth registry books digitised, 230,967 records; over 7,500 registry books catalogued, more than 1.3 million records, in five regions

systems.owner: Ministry of Justice and Human Rights, with UNDP and EU support
systems.tiers: periodic mobile operations in remote communities, combining legal aid and civil registration

systems.system: SIREC interoperability with national ID card, voter register, social protection and judiciary
systems.tiers: described as future, not in place

note: The report gives 19,142 new birth registrations and 627 marriage registrations for 2025 without saying they were made in SIREC, and gives no count of offices using it; no events, made or offices fact taken.
